Field observations suggest that parturition events are synchronized with local food availability, ensuring that the lactating female has access to adequate fruit resources to support the energetic demands of milk production for her single offspring.

The 73.8-gram weaning weight also appears to be a critical threshold, below which post-weaning survival rates in wild populations drop precipitously due to the energetic challenges of independent flight and fruit processing.
